account:
It is noon on day 0, and I have returned home for my scheduled lunch after the market walk. The clearest unusual item was hearing Townsfolk 03 and 23 repeat 'bridge or port change at inn.' I do not know what prompted that phrase or whether anything is actually changing. I asked the secretary to investigate and report at our one o'clock accounts appointment. The baker subsequently told me that freight had seen no bridge or port change and had merely offered delivery help, warehouse space, and ferry service. That is the baker's report of freight's words, not something I heard freight explain directly. It may be ordinary commercial arrangements being repeated as a rumor; I have no evidence of a secret plan.

Several market residents repeated that they had seen the baker carrying wheat at the bakery. I also saw the baker putting bread in the stall chest. The baker says business is well supplied, with seventy-two fresh loaves, and asked whether upcoming gatherings would need bread. The secretary said none are listed today or tomorrow. These observations fit normal baking and trade; I cannot infer a shortage or unusual gathering from them.

The builder approached during morning office hours carrying a lantern. I requested a repair inspection and estimate and invited the builder on the market walk, but no repair scope or price has been agreed and no spending is authorized. The secretary has correctly reinforced that limit. I have no grounds to connect the builder's work with the inn rumor.

My next useful step is to keep the one o'clock accounts appointment and hear what the secretary actually learned. Later I have tea at the dockside cottage at three and office hours at half past four. I want to understand town business without treating repeated hearsay as established fact.
